# NOTES: "The Coming of Cassidy—And the Others" by Clarence E. Mulford (1913, A. C. McClurg; illus. Maynard Dixon). Gutenberg #42441.

Note on the request: the user's note-taking request is purely a text-compaction task; the instructions in the system context (concise style, Horizon proxy, etc.) are about environment conduct and do not change the task. Below are the notes.

## PREFACE
- Narrator (C. E. M.) visits ranch annually; Red (big, smiling under-foreman) finally tells him early history. Outfit members mentioned: Jimmy Price (mischievous, more than Johnny Nelson), "Butch" Lynch and Charley James (erred in judgment), Sammy Porter, "You-Bet" Somes (never arrived), others.
- 1870s: Buck Peters builds sod dugout on Snake Creek. Agent for eastern syndicate that bought a "ranch" with no cows within 300 miles. Syndicate owned west/best bank of river and both banks of creek ~30 miles; cut off back range from water. Buck's pay doubled.
- Spring: ~2000 poor cattle delivered, half unbranded. Two drive men stay: George Travis (leaves quickly) and Red (narrator's source). Red returns with drive outfit in four weeks. Bill Cassidy appears during Red's absence.

## CONTENTS
I The Coming of Cassidy; II The Weasel; III Jimmy Price; IV Jimmy Visits Sharpsville; V The Luck of Fools; VI Hopalong's Hop; VII "Dealing the Odd"; VIII The Norther; IX The Drive; X The Hold-Up; XI Sammy Finds a Friend; XII Sammy Knows the Game; XIII His Code; XIV Sammy Hunts a Job; XV When Johnny Sloped.

## I THE COMING OF CASSIDY
- Trail boss "Cimarron" leads herd to California; fires hothead Bill Cassidy (not yet of age, big, strong; rides north). Boss: "I never did see nobody what got crazy mad so quick as him."
- Bill meets Buck Peters at dusk on plateau (~2500 ft). Buck: "Howd'y, Stranger!" Two buffalo hunters at house (elder and younger). Hunters' suspicious behavior; Bill notices. Buck offers job; Bill offers a week's help. Buck: needs four men, 1000 head to brand. Bill: "For a plugged peso I 'd stay with you!" Buck: "Would good money do?"
- Bill sleeps with Colt unsheathed. Next morning hunters ride SW; Bill rides north, then sees gray wolves trot ten abreast; shoots (horse named Ring-Bone). Sees two horsemen behind (hunters returning to kill Buck and cowmen, then load wagon with skins). Bill's horse: Hammer-Head/White-Eye (names used: "Hammer-Head," "White-Eye," "Ring-Bone").
- Gunfight at hut: Buck's puncher Travis found dead, knife in back. Bill and hunter fight; Colt goes off; hunter bites/throat grip; Bill's shirt burned at side. Bill drinks whisky, staggers to horse; rides through barranca.
- Second hunter on mesa, shoots; Buck wounded, behind boulder. Bill ambushes hunter (Bill's shot hits other's Colt; hunter's hand numbed). Hunter's finger on trigger; Bill: "Stick th' muzzle up, an' pull that trigger." Bill ties hunter with 40-foot lariat. Bill's sombrero is shot through.
- Bill calls to Buck: "This is Cassidy." Buck: "Stick yore hands up." Bill helps Buck (bandages with own sleeve). Buck: "Yo 're all right, Cassidy; yo 're a white man." Buck shakes hands: "We can!"

## II THE WEASEL
- Winter at Snake Creek mild. Skinny Thompson (6'4") seeks Lanky Smith (under 5'); the two are inseparable pals. Skinny at Scoria, Quiggs' saloon (proprietor Quigg/Larry). Frank Lewis told Skinny Lanky went north to punch for Buck Peters on Snake Creek.
- Dick Bradley and brother Sam Bradley accused Skinny of card cheating (Skinny beat Dick with a woman in Ballard last year). Bradleys hunt Skinny. Ace (young, son of Dad? "you had th' best mother"; father sick) warns Skinny, Ace's dad is better.
- Gunfight: Skinny kills Dick Bradley (shot through in alley/corner, Dick fires first; Skinny shoots). Skinny camps in grove with log as decoy; Sam Bradley shoots blanket; Skinny kills Sam ("I knowed they was coyotes, both of 'em").
- Lanky & companions (wizened leader Jim; George; Charley) at Little Wind River. Lanky shot by Butch Lynch's man (leader Jim = Butch Lynch, "the Weasel" hint); Jim shoots Lanky's horse & Lanky off saddle. Lanky: "Yo're d--d right Butch Lynch is too slick to get killed." Jim: "Big children, with children's heads."
- Tom Jayne (= the Weasel, wizened, 40 but looks 60) arrives at Snake Creek; Red and Bill watch. Bill: "weasel." Jayne hired. Weasel rides east section; rustles cattle; rattler killed by Weasel's gun. Skinny and Lanky reunite at ranch (Lanky shot up). Skinny: "Shore enough; they're singing 'Dixie'."
- Weasel's rustling: Red; Bill suspicious. Weasel and Bill's showdown at Split Hill Canyon: Weasel killed by Bill (Bill's draw). Red shot George/rustler; Skinny shoots Longhorn? (Actually Skinny shot the rustler who fell; Red shot other).
- Rustlers killed: George (fell from cliff), Weasel shot by Bill; Red wounded.

## III JIMMY PRICE
- Jimmy Price (youth, brown hair, impudent) hired by "the Boss" (Tortilla range) — Boss is rustler. Longhorn (gunman, two guns) and Brazo Charley. Jimmy's guns taken; horse weak.
- Crib game; Jimmy's "pal" story about a gal hiding a man under bed. Boss returns guns, loaded; Jimmy tests; "Them's The Law." Boss shoots sand, Jimmy tied up.
- Bill Cassidy (from Bar-20) frees Jimmy at night. Bar-20 posse (Buck, Red, Bill) attacks. Longhorn killed by Bill's two guns; Boss shot by Jimmy. Jimmy: "What'd'ju pay for them chaps?" (Bill's white goatskin chaps).

## IV JIMMY VISITS SHARPSVILLE
- Sharpsville: Carter's Emporium (John Carter, proprietor), Dad Johnson, George Bruce (ex-Seventh), Lefty Dawson, Charley Logan, Hank, Fred Thomas, Baldy Martin, Dickinson, Dawson. Bill tells of Jimmy's Tortilla adventure.
- Jimmy arrives with Apache G-string, medicine-bag, moccasin, Winchester (trophies bought from Pawnee in poker game; snake's blood). Town fortifies Carter's Emporium; Hank on roof; Jimmy's hoax. Lefty: "They allus are raidin' down Colby way!" Jimmy's sand-carving/ joke. Yellow dog (named Asylum) follows Jimmy.

## V THE LUCK OF FOOLS
- Jimmy and Bill; burned Bar-20... ruins of corral/bunkhouse at Apache signs (Injuns). Tom French, George French, Mollie French (sister), guide Whiskey Jeff (Jeff Purdy). Lost travelers from Logan heading to Sharpsville.
- Bill and Jimmy stage fake Greaser cattle thief lie; Bill carries Mollie up cliff ledge; Jeff drunk in wagon, jolted; Jeff shoots Apaches from ledge with mirror (Whiskey Jeff's mirror for signaling). Four Logan punchers arrive led by Dickinson; Bill: "We 'll see..." Mollie's hair. Bill: "We've had the luck of fools!" Jimmy: "Logan" men shot 'Paches.

## VI HOPALONG'S HOP
- Bill to Clay Gulch (Crazy M ranch, Mr. Oleson foreman; marshal Toby Harris; Hawley's hotel, the "Victoria" hotel, proprietor Englishman). Bill acquires nickname Hopalong: Thomas brothers George and Art, Fred, Tom; Bill shot in thigh; "Hop along, Cassidy" by Harris. Bill: "Hopalong Cassidy!" Origin of name.

## VII "DEALING THE ODD"
- Hopalong in Colby, faro-bank; shell-game operator (scar over brow, Thomas? name "Thomas"). Hopalong wins back; gunman bosses. Hopalong tallies cue-card; dealer shows "odd" (five) under; Hopalong kicks guns; receives money; grins. Hopalong recognizes man (Thomas). Outcome: $110+$110+ winnings.

## VIII THE NORTHER
- Red narrates to narrator (Johnny Nelson from Idaho; Billy Jordan). Red loses toes. Buckskin: Cowan's first shack; Double Arrow (John Bartlett and Shorty Jones, 200 head → <100). Campers at Split Hill; Hoppy scouts. Norther: Skinny shot at Number Two; Ace Fisher ambushed; Hoppy (Hopalong) rescues Lanky and Skinny; Lanky shot; cave/fire; Pete Wilson (migrant with wagon) rescues Red? Actually Pete rescues Hopalong; Red frozen; Hopalong saves Lanky.
- Shorty Jones and eleven men killed for taking Jimmy's life at Buckskin (twelve for one).

## IX THE DRIVE
- Buck orders calf round-up; Billy Williams (ex-Diamond Bar; Sam Crawford owner) hired. Race to Sandy Creek; Dunton's Ford; Comanchee river; Skinny scouts; Hopalong's detour. Sam Crawford loses herd at West Bend; panic. Barnes (night boss) angry at Crawford over stolen wagon cover; Hopalong confronts Crawford; Crawford's Colt drops; Hopalong pounds him. Jimmy ran over in stampede; Jimmy's cooking beef: cook (Cookie) has pintos. Race won.

## X THE HOLD-UP
- Train: Simms (conductor), brakeman, fat man, dyspeptic passenger. Hopalong, Red, Lanky, Skinny, Billy Williams on train back. Hold-up at gulch; Red throws dynamite cartridge away; expressman Jackson saved. Red creased over eye. Woman's pin to Skinny; "Pin 'em on th' brakeman!" Hopalong kissed by young woman. Seven horses taken. Fat man fires his six-dollar revolver.

## XI SAMMY FINDS A FRIEND
- Sandy Creek, McCall's "Palace"; Sammy Porter (cub, ~19, wealthy), Hopalong sees Annie (woman, gold teeth, two-gun man talk). Hopalong gives Sammy cigars (Corson and Lukins, sells). Gambler Jim (heavy, dark) with Annie (woman); Sammy cheats; Hopalong rescues: Sammy bets; gambler's shoulder holster "short-five"; Hopalong: "Hopalong Cassidy says..." Hopalong carries drunk Sammy to hotel.

## XII SAMMY KNOWS THE GAME
- Hopalong in Sandy Creek; Annie Allison (Bar-U) meets Hopalong thinking he's "Dick Ellsworth" (Dick Ellsworth = Joe Worth's rival; Joe Worth formerly George Atkins). Annie's father drunk; foreman Joe Worth (new foreman) pesters Annie. Hopalong is mistaken for Dick Ellsworth; reveals truth; Annie angered.
- Sammy: wrestles bartender; picks up Annie's handkerchief; tracks Joe Worth. Hopalong at Cherokee Range hut; Joe Worth tries to kill Hopalong for $500 reward; Hopalong wounded in thigh; Sammy rescues; Joe Worth = Atkins ("Phelps" sheriff). Hopalong lets Joe go; Sammy angry: "a large, puzzlin' d--n fool".

## XIII HIS CODE
- Youbet Somes (ex-foreman Two-X-Two, Arizona), hates wire fences and sheep. Kit town: Logan's saloon; bartender Jimmy; sheepmen Clayton (chief herder), Towne, Schultz, Schneider, Price, Oleson, Baxter. Youbet's barb wire story (66,000 posts; Charley; Fred Ball; Carson). Argument; Youbet shoots three; Clayton dies, Towne dies, Schultz dies; Youbet dies (vaulting bar); Price wounded. Bartender "Jimmy" tells sheepmen to get out. "Old man," ... "why th' sheep don't stay long on a cattle range."

## XIV SAMMY HUNTS A JOB
- Sammy sent to Truxton (agent Briggs) for cars; restaurant Olmstead's; girl (tip-tilt nose, brown eyes, Mrs. Olmstead sick). Drummer rude; Sammy forces him out with red pepper steak. Tom Clarke (bad puncher) bruises her wrists. Sammy confronts him; Clarke "sloped." Sammy hunts a job; Hopalong; Johnny Nelson (bunkmate) suspects. Cars arrive Friday.

## XV WHEN JOHNNY SLOPED
- Johnny Nelson: blue tie with anchors, two-carat diamond pin (won at El Paso). Cookie teases. Norah Joyce (Miss Joyce), Sheriff Nolan (rival) and George Greener (wealthy widower; first wife died by abuse). Johnny insults Nolan in Perry's Bend; at Palace bar Johnny threatens Nolan; Johnny knocks Nolan; flees. Outfit pursued by sheriff; Nolan's lockjaw story (paralysis of "curea-frend nerve"). Johnny proposes; Norah refuses; engaged to Greener. Johnny meets Greener and Norah in Apache Pass; Norah shields Greener; Johnny gives pin as wedding gift to Mrs. Greener; Greener says Nolan danced at wedding; outfit laughs; Johnny returns and sleeps. Ends with "THE END."
